The Authentic Name of AŋraMainyu

Scholarly reference for AŋraMainyu

Avestan

𐬀𐬢𐬭𐬀 𐬨𐬀𐬌𐬥𐬌𐬌𐬎

The name in its original Avestan form. 𐬀𐬢𐬭𐬀 𐬨𐬀𐬌𐬥𐬌𐬌𐬎 → AŋraMainyu. Avestan distinguishes the velar nasal ŋ (𐬢) written here in aŋra. · Unicode restoration AngraMainyu simplifies the nasal to n. · The diphthongal ending -iiu is written with two i letters followed by u.

ASCII Constraint

ANGRAMAINYU

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

AŋraMainyu

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Punycode Encoding
aŋramainyu.com → xn--aramainyu-bxb.com

The non-ASCII characters in AŋraMainyu are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is AŋraMainyu. PUNICODEX does not claim this domain is available; always verify status with a registrar.

Tier Classification

Why AŋraMainyu is classified as Tier-2

The Zoroastrian form 𐬀𐬢𐬭𐬀 𐬨𐬀𐬌𐬥𐬌𐬌𐬎 preserves neither stress nor length in this Unicode restoration. This makes it a single-tier Tier-2 name — a faithful scholarly form, without the distinctive phonetic features that define Tier-1.
